headline: New benchmarks and statistical methods probe bias in omics analysis pipelines
label: Benchmarking Omics Analysis Methods
summary: Recent preprints test whether single-cell, spatial, and microbiome analysis methods generalize and avoid bias or data leakage.
synthesis: The common thread is rigorous, statistically grounded evaluation and construction of analysis methods across omics modalities. A standardized benchmark for virtual cell perturbation-response models tests generalization to unseen contexts, perturbations, and datasets, while a systematic study of single-cell batch integration metrics on synthetic scenarios introduces sBEE, which combines neighborhood composition and mixing. Normalization is addressed by a housekeeping-gene pipeline that uses cross-validation, stability, and Gini coefficient criteria to reduce data leakage in machine learning. Other items extend inference to spatial multi-sample differential expression (TESSERA), histological community-level association testing (DCAFA), theoretical bias derivations for microbiome log-ratio transforms, and survival mediation for high-dimensional proteogenomics (SMAHP). What is new is the explicit attention to bias, leakage, and generalization at each analytical stage rather than a shared biological finding.
